charts.name: Solomon Islands reference chart of accounts
charts.legal_reference: There is no legal chart of accounts in the texts read for Solomon Islands, and no text read names a standard setter or a framework for company accounts. This chart is original: four digits, blocked so that each range reaches one line of the IFRS-style statements below (IAS 1, expenses by nature), with the accounts a Solomon Islands trading company keeps — goods tax and sales tax collected, the net amount payable to the Inland Revenue Division, PAYE withheld, National Provident Fund contributions and withholding taxes payable.

numbering.legal_reference: Goods Tax Act section 75 asks the goods tax to be stated on the wholesale invoice; no text read states a numbering rule. `sequential` and the number format are conventions of this pack and not rules of the law.

tax_point.legal_reference: Sales Tax Act section 14: the tax is collected at the time of the sale on the whole amount of the value. Goods Tax Act section 42: payable within thirty days after the close of the month of the sale. `invoice_date` is the pack's approximation of the time of the sale; a credit sale of goods (sixty days to pay) is not modelled.

einvoicing.legal_reference: No structured e-invoice standard, Peppol profile or clearance system of the Inland Revenue Division was found in the texts read; the returns are paper forms (GT4, ST4) and the eTax service. `obligation` is `none` for want of a text, not on a finding that none exists.

not_taxed.legal_reference: Sales Tax Act (Cap. 125) section 3(1) charges the purchaser a tax on the use or consumption of the prescribed goods and services, and section 3(6) has the importer of prescribed goods pay it on entry; neither the Act nor the forms read give a line of form ST4 for a service bought from a supplier abroad. The pack therefore carries no purchase tax for it. This is a finding about the texts read, not a finding that nothing is owed: it is a gap recorded in the README.
